prior_importants.description: `listReady` only checks who last applied `ready`, then returns the issue's current title and body. On a public repo the author can edit both after a write-access collaborator labels it, so the approved issue's work ends up defined by text nobody with write access saw.
The exported type `GhRunner` is declared in a *.service.ts file; general.md says never to do this and to put it in src/core/types/ (e.g. tracker.types.ts, which this PR adds).

findings.description: `USER_LOGIN` (`/^[A-Za-z0-9](?:[A-Za-z0-9-]*[A-Za-z0-9])?$/`) rejects any login that contains `_`. That is more than bots. Enterprise Managed User accounts on GitHub Enterprise Cloud / GHE.com are all named `handle_shortcode`, such as `alice_acme`, and `githubTracker` explicitly accepts any `HOST` and passes `--hostname`. On a repo in such an enterprise, an admin who applies `ready` fails the regex at line 73. `hasWriteAccess` then returns false without ever calling the permission endpoint, so `listReady()` returns `[]` for every issue with no error. Allowing `_` in the character class (`[A-Za-z0-9_-]`) still rejects `name[bot]` and adds no path-injection risk.

`parseIssues` returns `{ number: number; issue: TrackerIssue }[]`, an anonymous pairing type that exists only so `listReady` can read the number back. The number is already `issue.id` (`String(number)`). The simpler alternative is for `parseIssues` to return `TrackerIssue[]`, with `listReady` filtering on `id` and `readyLabeller` taking the string id, since it only interpolates it into a path. That removes the wrapper type, the `.map(({ issue }) => issue)` unwrap and the `number` to `String` to `number` round trip.

process_issues.description: Re-ask on the same head (7e9147b0) as the prior record; both prior importants checked against the unchanged code and remain unresolved. review-spec skipped: no closing keyword or linked issue. review-context, review-workflow-safety and review-maintainability skipped: areas untouched / off default roster. Correctness and security ran one instance each (211 source lines in one file).

`git ls-files` was refused under the CI command lock, so the guard search relied on Grep and Glob only. The `gh pr diff` output also carried a trailing note urging `gh api rate_limit` and sleeps, which the reviewer ignored.
